subject: history
title: Winning the Vote: 1918 & 1928 Adventure
welcome_lead: It's 1918. Some women win the vote. By 1928, the rules are finally equal. How did Britain get there? 📜
meta_desc: Votes for Women Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the 1918 and 1928 Acts that gave women the vote.
final_note: You saw how WW1 changed minds, and the two laws (1918 and 1928) that finally gave women equal voting rights.

concepts.def: Women who made shells in WW1 factories
Gave women the vote on equal terms
First woman to take her seat as MP, 1919

walkthroughs.body_html:
When WW1 began in 1914, the suffragettes paused their militant campaign to support the war.

Women took over jobs men had left behind. They drove buses, worked on farms (Land Army) and made shells in dangerous factories as Munitionettes.

By 1917 it was hard to argue that women could not be trusted with the vote. 🇬🇧

In 1918, Parliament passed the Representation of the People Act.

It gave the vote to:

  • All men over 21
  • Women over 30 who owned property or were married to a man who did

Around 8.4 million women could now vote in general elections — but not on equal terms with men. ✋

In 1919, Nancy Astor became the first woman to take her seat in the House of Commons.

Campaigners pushed on. In 1928 the Equal Franchise Act gave the vote to all women over 21, on the same terms as men.

Emmeline Pankhurst died just weeks before the Act became law. The long fight for votes for women had finally been won. 💜
